A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 58 pages, including Appendices A–F, equations, figures, and tables, are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3.3–4 and Appendices C–F report original Gaussian-mixture simulations and CIFAR-10/Mini-ImageNet classification experiments.

after.justification: The original simulations and image-classification experiments remain in Sections 3.3–4 and Appendices C–F, including numerical results and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The empirical-mean classifier, dimension-reducing processing, and denoising/encoding procedures are unchanged. Equation 6 drops the explicit dataset argument from the estimated means and clarifies their class-specific estimation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture simulations, noisy CIFAR-10 and Mini-ImageNet classification tasks, and CIFAR-5m supplementation described in Appendix C. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Sections 4 and Appendices C–E retain the same comparisons: raw-image ResNet classifiers versus classification using DnCNN-denoised images or DINOv2-based embeddings with an MLP. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: The sample-size and class-imbalance grids, noise levels, preprocessing, classification-error and efficiency metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged in Sections 3.3–4 and Appendices C–F.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the SURE-denoiser experiments, training-versus-testing error analysis in Figure 4, and Appendix F studies of SNR, reduced dimension, and unlabeled sample counts. The geometric illustration in Figure 15 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: The reporting practices remain identical: 100 independent simulation trials, six classifier seeds for CIFAR-10 denoising, three seeds for Mini-ImageNet experiments, and the same mean/standard-deviation reporting and error bars.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains errors of 71.12 ± 1.39% without denoising and 63.32 ± 0.96% with denoising at 1,000 training samples, noise level 0.25, and balanced classes.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, theorem statements, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Simplified notation in Equation 6 and scalar-typeface corrections in Equations 42 and 45 do not change mathematical meaning or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about finite-sample benefits from preprocessing, dependence on class separation and training-data size/balance, and practical experiments exhibiting trends consistent with the theory.

C2.justification: The explanations of nonmonotonic efficiency, SNR and imbalance effects, and improved mean estimation remain unchanged. The qualification about encoding versus denoising for tasks requiring spatial information and the proposed extensions beyond the current theory are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices C–F retain the same architectures, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and processing details. The new acknowledgment concerns LLM use for writing polish and adds no technical implementation or experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged. The Hen et al. reference receives a different title and a 2026 rather than 2025 date, but retains the same authors and arXiv identifier 2511.18471; this is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: Limited edits specify 'mutual information' in Section 2, clarify the estimated means in Section 3.1, simplify notation, and update citation metadata. The acknowledgments add 'LLMs were used only to polish the writing.' Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header throughout and updates the arXiv margin stamp. Small text-spacing and equation-typesetting changes occur, but all 15 figures and four tables retain their content, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes small wording and notation clarifications, updates publication/reference metadata, and discloses LLM use for writing polish. These provide limited editorial benefits while leaving the arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged; they do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
